name: Paul Newman
keys: actor racing daytona cool hand luke
blurb: The blue-eyed standard for looking dressed without trying: Oxford shirts, navy blazers, chinos and loafers, worn with a racer's indifference to all of it.
signatureDesc: Navy blazer with white shirt, khaki trousers and brown loafers
rules: Effort is invisible or it is too much: the blazer is tailored, everything else is simply clean and fitted.
Blue eyes, blue wardrobe — navy, white and khaki carry nearly every look he ever wore.
One personal signature, kept for decades — his was the chronograph. Find yours and stop rotating.
avoid: Avoid: novelty, logos, and anything that looks bought for the photograph.

name: James Dean
keys: actor rebel without a cause jeans tee
blurb: Three films and one uniform: the white tee, the jean, the boot. Dean proved a silhouette and an attitude can be a whole wardrobe.
signatureDesc: White tee with indigo jeans and black boots
rules: Two pieces can be a look if both fit perfectly — the tee touches the arm, the jean sits on the boot.
Buy the plainest version of everything; the wearer is the decoration.
Never dress up the uniform. Dean in a suit is a costume; Dean in a tee is history.
avoid: Avoid: accessories, colour, and effort — all three break the spell.

name: Alain Delon
keys: actor french plein soleil purple noon
blurb: French cinema's beautiful coldness: dark tailoring, grey flannel, black loafers, and knitwear worn like armour. Plein Soleil is still the Riviera masterclass.
signatureDesc: Navy blazer with grey trousers and black loafers
rules: Dark, fitted, quiet: the French end of tailoring removes everything the Italian end adds.
Grey flannel is the Riviera trouser after six — white is for lunch.
Let one thing smoulder — the knit, the collar, the stare. The clothes stay plain.
avoid: Avoid: colour, pattern, and warmth of any obvious kind.

name: Marcello Mastroianni
keys: actor italian fellini dolce vita suit
blurb: Fellini's leading man: the black suit, the white shirt, the dark glasses. Mastroianni made formality look like it cost him no effort at all.
signatureDesc: Black blazer with white shirt and black trousers
rules: Black and white is a complete palette when the tailoring is Roman — soft shoulder, narrow trouser.
Formality worn loosely beats casual worn carefully: loosen the tie, never the standard.
Glasses are part of the outfit, not an afterthought — choose them like shoes.
avoid: Avoid: colour statements. Rome after dark is monochrome.

name: Fred Astaire
keys: dancer actor top hat classic hollywood
blurb: The most natural tailor-wearer ever filmed: soft suits, button-down collars, a tie used as a belt, and shoes he could dance in. Elegance as movement.
signatureDesc: Grey blazer with white shirt, navy trousers and brown shoes
rules: Tailoring must move: if you can't dance in it, the cut is wrong, however it photographs.
Small improvisations are the signature — a scarf through the belt loops, a tie for a belt. One per look.
Brown suede shoes forgive almost any suit and dress down almost any formality.
avoid: Avoid: stiffness — in cloth, in collar, in manner.

name: Duke of Windsor
keys: edward viii king prince of wales check royal
blurb: The abdication king who dressed better than anyone on either throne: Prince of Wales check, fair isle knits, plus-fours, and patterns mixed with total confidence.
signatureDesc: Grey checked blazer with grey trousers and brown shoes
rules: Pattern is a skill, not a risk: checks over stripes work when the scales differ and the colours agree.
Invent your own combinations and repeat them for decades — that is how a style becomes a signature.
Comfort is royal: soft construction, room to move, nothing pinched in the name of formality.
avoid: Avoid: plainness as a default. The Duke never wore an unconsidered outfit in his life.

name: David Gandy
keys: model british dolce gabbana three piece
blurb: The model who brought the three-piece suit and the knitted polo back to British menswear: sharp tailoring, textured knits, and grooming treated as part of the outfit.
signatureDesc: Navy blazer with white knit polo, grey trousers and brown loafers
rules: Texture is the modern pattern: a knitted polo or a flecked tweed does the work a print used to do.
The waistcoat is not costume when the fit is current — close, clean, and worn with confidence.
Grooming is a garment: hair, skin and nails finished to the same standard as the suit.
avoid: Avoid: anything baggy. Gandy's whole register is fit.

name: Idris Elba
blurb: Big-frame tailoring kept minimal: dark suits, black knits, everything close and clean. Proof that restraint scales — the fewer the pieces, the sharper the man.
signatureDesc: Charcoal blazer with black knit and charcoal trousers
rules: When the frame is big, the clothes go quiet: dark, plain, and cut close.
A black knit under a charcoal blazer is a full evening look — no shirt, no tie, no apology.
Fit is the whole statement at this register; a loose seam reads louder than any pattern.
avoid: Avoid: bright colour and busy detail — both fight the silhouette.

name: George Clooney
blurb: The silver standard: Italian-cut dark suits, open-collar shirts, and the discipline of never once being photographed in a bad outfit across thirty years.
signatures: No tie unless the room demands it
signatureDesc: Charcoal blazer with light blue shirt and grey trousers
rules: Own one perfect dark suit before five good ones — Clooney's wardrobe reads like a single decision repeated.
The open collar is earned by the tailoring underneath it; sloppy shirt, no shortcut.
Grey is a strategy, not a phase: knit, hair and tailoring in the same family reads intentional.
avoid: Avoid: trends entirely. Nothing he wears has a season attached to it.

name: Brad Pitt
keys: actor once upon hollywood linen relaxed
blurb: Tailoring loosened by California: linen suits, cream and tan, tees under blazers, and loafers worn like slippers. Formality with the tension let out.
signatureDesc: Tan blazer with white tee, cream trousers and brown loafers
rules: Unstructured everything: the Californian suit has no padding and no agenda.
Cream and tan are a full wardrobe in the sun — vary the texture, not the colour.
A white tee under a blazer is the house uniform; the blazer must be soft or the trick fails.
avoid: Avoid: dark formality in daylight. This register lives in the sun.

name: Ryan Gosling
blurb: The modern knitwear icon: statement jumpers, burgundy and cream, boots with tailoring, and one unforgettable satin bomber. Colour confidence without costume.
signatureDesc: Burgundy knit with navy trousers and brown boots
rules: One statement piece per look — the knit, the jacket — and everything else plain enough to frame it.
Burgundy is the modern neutral for evening: richer than navy, calmer than black.
Boots under trousers sharpen a knit look from cosy to deliberate.
avoid: Avoid: two statements at once. The bomber and the knit never share a look.

name: Nick Wooster
keys: street style pitti camo blazer moustache
blurb: Pitti's pattern-clasher: a tailored blazer over camo, shorts with tailoring, tattoos under tweed. Rules mastered so thoroughly he can break three at once.
signatureDesc: Checked blazer with olive trousers and brown shoes
rules: Clash patterns by scale, never by colour family: camo and check agree in olive, grey and brown.
One tailored piece makes street clothes a look — the blazer is doing the diplomacy.
Shorts can be tailored. The rule is the crease, not the length.
avoid: Avoid: playing safe. Wooster's register is the considered collision.

name: Lapo Elkann
keys: fiat italian dandy denim suit eccentric
blurb: Agnelli's grandson and heir to the eccentricity: denim double-breasted suits, wraparound colour, and sprezzatura pushed to theatre — deliberately, every time.
signatureDesc: Indigo denim blazer with white shirt, indigo jeans and brown loafers
rules: Eccentricity is a discipline: the denim suit is tailored like a suit, or it is just jeans twice.
One electric accent — orange, turquoise — against an otherwise classic base.
Inherit the rules, then bend them in public. That is the family business.
avoid: Avoid: half-measures. This register commits or it doesn't work.

name: Roger Federer
blurb: The court classicist off court: cream knits, navy tailoring, white sneakers kept immaculate, and tailoring as precise as the backhand was.
signatureDesc: Cream knit polo with navy trousers and white sneakers
rules: Sporting clothes, tailored fit: the polo and the knit are cut like shirts, not souvenirs.
White sneakers are only a look when they are spotless — maintenance is the style.
Navy and cream cover nearly every occasion between the club and dinner.
avoid: Avoid: logos worn large. The sponsor era is over; the clothes speak plainly now.

name: Robert Redford
blurb: Sundance ease: denim shirts, tan jackets, jeans and boots, with a blazer thrown over the whole Western wardrobe when the occasion asked.
signatureDesc: Tan jacket with denim shirt, indigo jeans and brown boots
rules: Denim is a shirt, a trouser and a jacket — just never all three at full strength.
Tan and indigo is the Western palette; brown boots finish everything in it.
Rugged pieces, clean presentation: the boots are worn, the man is groomed.
avoid: Avoid: polish. This register is sun and dust, tailored lightly.

name: Humphrey Bogart
blurb: Casablanca's silhouette: the trench coat, the soft fedora, the suit underneath kept simple. Noir dressing is a coat, a hat, and total commitment.
signatureDesc: Tan coat with grey trousers and black shoes
rules: The coat is the look: everything under a trench can be a plain dark suit and still read iconic.
A hat is a decision, not an accessory — wear it like you mean it or leave it home.
Noir is restraint in shadow colours: tan, grey, black, and one white shirt.
avoid: Avoid: colour and novelty. Rick's café runs in monochrome.
